Rashi on Shabbat 113b:10:1.hebrew: מצד הקוצרים - כל הקוצרים הפסיקו בינו לבינה, ולא הושיבה בתוכם או אצלו. רוח הקדש נזרקה בו, ולרמז שמלכות בית דוד היוצאת משניהם עתידה ליחלק, דאילו ישבה בתוכם לא היה זה רמז הפסקה בין שניהם:
Rashi on Shabbat 113b:10:1.english: Beside the harvesters - All the harvesters separated between him and her, and he did not seat her among them or next to him. The Divine Spirit was cast upon him, and [this was] to hint that the kingdom of the House of David, which descends from both of them, is destined to be divided, for if she had sat among them, this would not have been a hint of a separation between the two of them.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:11:1.hebrew: ותאכל ותשבע - לשון עושר הוא. דוד, שלמה וחזקיה כתיב בהן עושר, שהיו מביאים להן כל מלכי ארץ מנחה:
Rashi on Shabbat 113b:11:1.english: And she ate, and she was satiated - [This] is an expression of wealth. [Regarding] David, Solomon, and Hezekiah, wealth is written of them, for all the kings of the earth would bring them tribute.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:11:2.english: His horsekeeper [ahuriyarei] - Appointed over his horses and mules.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:12:1.hebrew: ותחת כבודו - איידי דאיירי בקרא בפלוגתא דרבי יוחנן ור"א ורבי שמואל בר נחמני, נקטיה להאי הכא:
Rashi on Shabbat 113b:12:1.english: And under his honor - Since [the Gemara] is dealing with the verse in the dispute of Rabbi Yochanan, Rabbi Elazar, and Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani, it cited this [passage] here.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:12:2.hebrew: ה"ג רבי יוחנן אומר: תחת כבודו, ולא כבודו ממש; רבי יוחנן לטעמיה, דר"י קרי למאניה מכבדותי. רא"א: תחת כבודו ממש. ר' שמואל בר נחמני אומר: תחת כבודו כשריפת בני אהרן כו' - והכי פירושא: בין לרבי יוחנן בין לר"א גופן נשרף, אלא רבי יוחנן משמע ליה "תחת כבודו" כמו "תחת רגליו", לשון תחתית, ו"כבודו" היינו בגדיו, וה"ק: תחת בגדיהם של חיילותיו של סנחריב יקד יקוד, ולא בגדיהם נשרפו. ור"א משמע ליה "תחת" לשון חליפין, כמו "ישלם תחת השור" (שמות כ״א:ל״ז), משום דר"א לא קרי למאני' מכבדותיה, לכך ע"כ "כבודו" היינו גופו, וה"ק: כבודו ממש ישרף, ותחתיו יהא אפר ושריפה כיקוד אש. ורבי שמואל משמע ליה "תחת" כר' יוחנן, ו"כבודו" כר"א; הלכך קרא כר' יוחנן מידרש, ותחת כבודו נשרף ולא כבודו ממש, והאי "כבודו" גופו הוא, והלכך כשריפת בני אהרן — שריפת נשמה וגוף קיים, כדאמרינן בסנהדרין בד' מיתות (סנהדרין ד' נב.):
Rashi on Shabbat 113b:12:2.english: This is how we read [the Gemara]: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: "Under his honor," and not his actual honor; Rabbi Yoḥanan follows his own reasoning, for Rabbi Yoḥanan called his clothing "my honor." Rabbi Elazar says: "[In place of] his actual honor." Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani says: "Under his honor" is like the burning of the sons of Aaron, etc. - And this is the explanation: according to both Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Elazar, their bodies were burned; however, Rabbi Yoḥanan understands "under his honor" as like "under his feet," an expression of being underneath, and "his honor" refers to his clothing, and this is what [the verse] is saying: underneath the clothing of Sennacherib's troops a burning shall burn, and their clothing was not burned. Whereas Rabbi Elazar understands "under" as an expression of exchange, as in "he shall pay [an ox] for (lit. under) the ox" (Exodus 21:37), because Rabbi Elazar does not call his clothing "his honor"; therefore, perforce "his honor" refers to his body, and this is what [the verse] is saying: his actual honor shall be burned, and in its place there shall be ashes and burning like a burning fire. And Rabbi Shmuel understands "under" like Rabbi Yoḥanan, and "his honor" like Rabbi Elazar; therefore, the verse is expounded like Rabbi Yoḥanan — that underneath his honor was burned and not his actual honor — and this "honor" is his body, and therefore [it was] like the burning of the sons of Aaron — burning of the soul while the body remains intact — as we say in Sanhedrin in [the chapter] Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 52a).

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:1:1.english: That your speech on Shabbat should not be like your speech during the week - For example, buying and selling, and accounts.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:1:2.hebrew: הרהור מותר - להרהר בלבו, כך וכך יציאות אני צריך להוציא על שדה זו:
Rashi on Shabbat 113b:1:2.english: Contemplating [weekday affairs] is permitted - To think in one's heart, "Such and such expenses I need to spend on this field."

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:1:3.english: If he can place his first foot - [that is, the foot] that he lifted from this side to place on that side.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:1:4.hebrew: קודם שתעקר שניה - שאין רחבה יותר מכדי פסיעה, ורגלו אחת לצד זה ושניה לצד זה:
Rashi on Shabbat 113b:1:4.english: Before the second [foot] is lifted - [Meaning] that its width is not more than the span of a step, and one of his feet is on this side and the second [is] on that side.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:1:5.english: It is permitted - Even to jump and to lift this [second foot] before the first [one] has come to rest.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:2:1.english: [Should] he go around - to the place where the stream ends.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:2:2.english: Should he cross - That he should place his foot in the water.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:2:3.english: Sometimes his clothes will become soaked - They will be soaked in water.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:2:5.hebrew: מהו לפסוע פסיעה גסה - מי עבר משום מעשות דרכיך? פסיעה גסה יותר מאמה, פסיעה בינונית אמה:
Rashi on Shabbat 113b:2:5.english: What is [the ruling] regarding taking a large stride - Does one transgress on account of "from pursuing your ways"? A large stride [is] more than a cubit; an average stride [is] a cubit.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:2:6.english: Kiddush of twilight - [This refers to] one who drinks from the wine of Kiddush on Shabbat nights.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:3:1.hebrew: מהו לאכול אדמה - ארזיל"א בלע"ז. מי גזרו בה משום שחיקת סמנים כשאר רפואה, או לא:
Rashi on Shabbat 113b:3:1.english: What is [the law regarding] eating earth - Argile in Old French [clay]. Did they decree [a prohibition] against it due to grinding herbs, like other remedies, or not?

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:3:2.english: That it is harmful - [It] brings [one] to illness.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:3:3.english: From the flesh of his ancestors - Who died there in exile.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:3:4.hebrew: שקצים ורמשים - הא ודאי אתמחוי אתמחו ולא נעשו עפר?:
Rashi on Shabbat 113b:3:4.english: Abominations and creeping creatures - But surely they were completely dissolved [in the Flood] and did not become dust?

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:4:1.english: Rather, since it is harmful - they decreed regarding it on account of eating abominations and creeping creatures.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:4:2.english: Cress sprouted in him - The cress took root in the earth [that he had eaten], grew in his innards, touched his heart, and he died.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:5:1.hebrew: שמלותיך - וכי ערומה היתה? אלא שמלות מיוחדות, והיינו דשבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 113b:5:1.english: Your robes - Was she then naked? Rather, [it means] special robes, and that is [what is meant by garments] of Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:6:1.hebrew: ותרד הגורן והדר ותעש - שם סכה ולבשה שמלות נאות, שלא יפגשו בה כשהיא מקושטת ויאמרו זונה היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 113b:6:1.english: "And she went down to the threshing floor," and afterward, "and she did" - There she anointed [herself] and put on fine garments, so that [people] would not encounter her while she was adorned and say, "She is a harlot."

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:6:2.hebrew: שמואל - שהיתה שכינה קוראה לו מתוך ההיכל, ולא היה יודע מי קורא לו, וכתיב התם: "ויבן עלי כי ה' קורא לנער ויאמר לו לך שכב והיה אם יקרא אליך ואמרת דבר ה' כי שומע עבדך". והוא לא רצה להזכיר השם, שמא אין זו שכינה:
Rashi on Shabbat 113b:6:2.english: Samuel - For the Divine Presence was calling to him from within the Sanctuary, and he did not know who was calling to him. And it is written there: "And Eli understood that the Lord was calling the boy, and he said to him: Go, lie down, and it shall be, if He calls to you, you shall say: Speak, Lord, for Your servant is listening." And he did not want to mention the [Divine] Name, lest it not be the Divine Presence.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:7:1.english: Suitable people - [Those] among the harvesters, to walk with them.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:7:2.hebrew: לישאל בנערה - כל נערות שרואה היה דרכו לישאל מי הן? א"כ, מסתכל בהן היה:
Rashi on Shabbat 113b:7:2.english: To inquire about a young woman - All young women whom he saw — was it his habit to inquire who they were? If so, he would have been gazing at them!

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:7:3.hebrew: שני שבלין לקטה - כשהיא רואה שני שבלין שנפלו מן הקוצרים, לוקטתן; אבל שלש שוכבות יחד, אין לוקטתן, דהכי היא מתניתין (פאה פ"ו משנה ה): שני שבלים לקט, ג' אינו לקט:
Rashi on Shabbat 113b:7:3.english: Two stalks she collected - When she sees two stalks that fell from the harvesters, she collects them; however, [when] three are lying together, she does not collect them, for thus is the Mishnah (Peah 6:5): two stalks are gleanings, three are not gleanings.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:8:1.hebrew: עומדות - שבלים עומדות ששכח בועז, לוקטת מעומד, דשכחת קמה נמי הוי שכחה:
Rashi on Shabbat 113b:8:1.english: Upright - Standing stalks that Boaz forgot, she gleaned while standing, for forgotten standing grain is also [considered] forgotten sheaves.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:8:2.hebrew: נופלות - אותן שנשרו מן הקוצרים, לוקטת מיושב ואינה שחה ליטלן משום צניעות:
Rashi on Shabbat 113b:8:2.english: Fallen - Those [ears of grain] that fell from the harvesters, she gathers while sitting, and she does not bend over to take them out of modesty.

Rashi on Shabbat 113b:9:1.english: He hinted to her - The Holy Spirit was instilled in him.

Tosafot on Shabbat 113b:1:1.hebrew: שלא יהא דבורך של שבת כדבורך של חול - פי' בקונטרס: כגון מקח וממכר. ואין נראה לר"ת, דהא כבר נפקא מ"מצוא חפצך"; אלא אומר ר"ת: כדאמר בויקרא רבה (פ' לד): ר"ש בן יוחי הוה ליה אימא סבתא דהות מישתעיא סגיא, אמר לה: "אימא, שבתא הוא", שתקה. משמע שאין כל כך לדבר בשבת כמו בחול. ובירושל' אמרי': בטורח התירו בשאלת שלום בשבת:
Tosafot on Shabbat 113b:1:1.english: That your speech on Shabbat should not be like your speech during the week - The Kunteres [Rashi] explained: such as [discussing] buying and selling. But this does not seem [correct] to Rabbeinu Tam, for that is already derived from "pursuing your affairs" [Isaiah 58:13]. Rather, Rabbeinu Tam says [that it means] as it states in Vayikra Rabbah (Parashah 34): Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai had an elderly mother who would speak excessively; he said to her, "Mother, it is Shabbat," [and] she fell silent. This implies that one should not speak as much on Shabbat as during the week. And in the Yerushalmi they say: With difficulty did they permit greeting [one another with] shalom on Shabbat.
